questions.q: What does torchrun's --nnodes=1:64 flag actually express in an elastic launch?
options: The job will always use exactly 64 nodes and fail if any node is missing
The job is allowed to run with anywhere from 1 to 64 nodes, continuing at a reduced size rather than failing outright if nodes drop out
The job requires 64 separate launches, one per node
The job will automatically scale up to 1:64 ratio of GPUs to CPUs
questions.explain: The min:max syntax defines an allowed range of node counts the elastic job can operate within, rather than a fixed requirement — letting it continue at reduced scale if nodes are lost.

questions.q: What role does the c10d rendezvous backend play when a Worker node disappears mid-training?
options: It permanently deletes the job's state to force a clean restart
It lets surviving ranks re-discover each other and agree on a new, smaller group membership without any human re-launching the job
It automatically provisions a replacement GPU instance
It converts the job from PyTorch to a different framework
questions.explain: c10d is the rendezvous mechanism that allows the remaining ranks to tear down the old process group and re-form a new one with the updated membership, entirely in software, without manual intervention.

questions.q: After surviving ranks re-form the process group following a Worker failure, where does training resume from?
options: From step zero, as if the job were starting fresh
From exactly the in-flight step that was running when the Worker disappeared
From the last saved checkpoint, since in-memory state on the survivors was built for the old world size and must be reloaded against the new one
Training cannot resume at all after any rank failure
questions.explain: The in-flight step is lost (there's no resuming mid-collective), so the reformed group reloads state from the most recent checkpoint via dcp.load rather than starting over or magically preserving the exact in-flight computation.

questions.q: What does --max-restarts=3 protect against in an elastic training job?
options: It limits the job to exactly 3 total training steps
It caps how many times the elastic agent will attempt to re-form the group before giving up and marking the job genuinely Failed, protecting against a flapping node looping forever
It restricts the job to 3 GPUs maximum
It sets the maximum checkpoint file size to 3 gigabytes
questions.explain: Without a cap, a node that keeps getting reclaimed and rejoining could cause the elastic agent to retry re-formation indefinitely. max-restarts bounds that retry behavior.

questions.q: Why does Solara AI set the practical floor of --nnodes well above 1, even though the syntax allows it?
options: Because torchrun technically forbids values below 8
Because training a 70B-parameter model on a handful of nodes would be so slow that it's not worth continuing, versus waiting for replacement capacity and resuming from checkpoint at full scale
Because checkpoints can only be loaded onto exactly 64 nodes
Because NCCL requires a minimum of 32 nodes to initialize at all
questions.explain: Elastic training's range sets both a ceiling and, practically, a floor — continuing at too small a scale may be so inefficient that it's better to pause and resume at full capacity once replacement nodes are available.
